---

I'm 64 years old this year, and I've been farming these fields in Quzhou for over 40 years. My family has about 13 mu of land — not a big farm, but it's what we have. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent says when he comes to the village, but at the end of the day I trust my own eyes and what my neighbors do more than any advice from outside.

This year, I'll put 9 mu into wheat–maize double cropping and 4 mu into cotton. I know this split well — most of us in the village do the same. Wheat and maize are my insurance: even if cotton prices drop or the bollworm hits hard, I'll still have grain to sell and eat. Cotton pays better when it works, but I'm getting older and my back isn't what it used to be. The bending and picking hurts, so I keep cotton to 4 mu. I can't afford to give it up entirely — my son works in town and sends some money, but we still need the cash from cotton for medical expenses and daily costs.

For wheat, I planted last October with rotary tillage, like I always do. I use improved seed — I used to save my own, but the yield difference is too obvious to ignore. I put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, which gives me roughly 12–13 kg of nitrogen, plus some phosphorus and potassium. The extension guy says I should go to 15 kg nitrogen, but I've tried that and didn't see much difference, so I stick with what works. I'll irrigate four times: winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Each time I pump water it costs me electricity money, so four times is enough — my neighbor Lao Zhang does five, but I think he wastes money. For pests, I'll spray herbicide once and insecticide two or three times depending on what I see in the field. I expect about 1100 jin per mu if the weather holds — last year I got close to that.

Maize is planted right after wheat harvest in early June. There's no time for tillage — the window is barely a week, sometimes less. I plant directly with no-tillage using hybrid seed, usually Denghai or Nongda varieties from the seed dealer. I don't add extra fertilizer for maize. The wheat residue and whatever is left in the soil is enough, and honestly I'm too busy and too short on cash to buy more. I'll irrigate maize twice — once at the big喇叭口 stage and once at filling — if the rains don't come. Two or three sprays for insects and weeds, that's it. I usually get about 1100 jin per mu for maize, sometimes a bit more.

Cotton goes on 4 mu. I rotary till those plots in April and plant improved cotton seed. I put down some compound fertilizer at planting — not too much, maybe 2 kg nitrogen worth per mu, with a little phosphorus and potassium. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll-setting, so I'll irrigate twice. The real pain is pesticide — I spray about 16 times through the season for bollworm, aphids, and red spider mite. It costs money and takes time, but if you skip even one spray you can lose the whole crop. I hire some help for spraying now because my shoulders can't carry the tank like they used to. I expect about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu if I'm lucky.

The tradeoff is always money versus yield. I could spend more on fertilizer and get a bit more grain, but at my age I prefer stability. I've seen too many farmers lose money chasing higher yields. I keep some cash in hand for emergencies — my wife's medicine, pump repairs, whatever comes up. This plan isn't fancy, but it's what I know works.
